name: 6.2 Supercharged V8
notes: Variant: MY2015 US-market Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat (non-Widebody; supercharged 6.2-liter HEMI Hellcat V-8, 6,166 cc, 707 bhp at 6,000 rpm, Max. Engine Speed 6,200 rpm) with the optional TorqueFlite 8HP90 eight-speed automatic (4.71/3.14/2.10/1.67/1.29/1.00/0.84/0.67, two decimals as printed by FCA) and the 2.62:1 asymmetric limited-slip final drive, on the standard 275/40ZR20 tyres (same size front and rear; the driven axle is the rear). Not modelled: the Tremec TR-6060 6-speed manual (3.70 axle), the Widebody (305/35ZR20), the Redeye/Super Stock (797/807 hp, 6,500 rpm) and the 3.09 axle; the MY2019-2023 FCA/Stellantis sheets rate the SRT Hellcat at 717 bhp but keep the 6,200 rpm max engine speed, the 8HP90 ratios, the 2.62 final drive and 275/40ZR20 tyres. Cylinder->bank: Chrysler numbering, odd cylinders 1-3-5-7 (front to rear) on the left/driver bank = bank 0 (the bank of cylinder 1), even cylinders 2-4-6-8 on the right/passenger bank = bank 1 (Mopar's harness layout puts 1-3-5-7 and 2-4-6-8 in separate banks with cylinder 1 at the front and its 'Bank 1' sensor on the left, OBD bank 1 being the bank of cylinder 1; Summit Racing's tech note gives 1-3-5-7 on the driver side). Combustion entries are listed in Mopar's firing order 1-8-4-3-6-5-7-2 at even 90-degree crank intervals, giving the per-bank pattern L-R-R-L-R-L-L-R (bank 0 at 0/270/450/540, bank 1 at 90/180/360/630). Cross-plane crank derived from that firing order: 8-4 and 5-7 fire the same bank in succession, which a flat-plane V8 (banks strictly alternating) cannot do. Supercharger: IHI 2,380 cc/rev Lysholm twin-screw with 3-lobe male / 5-lobe female rotors. FCA's 2.36:1 drive ratio is the belt drive (pulleyRatio 2.36) turning the low-speed rotor (2.36 x 6,200 = 14,632 rpm; FCA: 'maximum speed of 14,600 rpm'); the 3-lobe male rotor turns 5/3 as fast through the rotor timing gears (gearRatio 1.6667, first principles; SRT's chief engineer quotes 14,500 / 24,000 rpm for the low-/high-speed rotors), so the whine order pulleyRatio x gearRatio x 3 male lobes = 11.8 per engine revolution (= 2.36 x 5 female lobes). The lobe counts and rotor speeds come from secondary press (EngineLabs interview with SRT chief engineer Gregg Black); FCA's own press kit states twin-screw, 2,380 cc/rev, 2.36:1 and 14,600 rpm. shiftTimeS 0.16 s = FCA's '160 millisecond shifts' for the Hellcat's 8HP90 (2016 press kit). EPA: the MY2015 Test Car List row 'Challenger SRT8' (FCA US LLC, 6.2 L, 707 hp, 8-speed automatic with lockup, top gear ratio < 1, axle 2.62, N/V 21.1), carried over unchanged through MY2023, matches 8th gear (0.67 x 2.62 = 1.7554; FCA's 720.9 revs/mile x 1.7554 / 60 = 21.09); the model gives 21.22 rpm/mph (+0.6 %). Source conflicts: SAE Automotive Engineering (May 2014) names the automatic '845RE', while FCA's spec sheets and press kits call it the TorqueFlite 8HP90 (FCA used); FCA's 2017 sheet lists the 707 bhp at 6,200 rpm versus 6,000 rpm in the 2015 sheet (peak-power rpm is not used by the model). Estimated (not published in the sources used): idle 700 rpm; limiter type fuel-soft at the published 6,200 rpm max engine speed with 150 rpm hysteresis; torque converter stallRpmWot 2,500 rpm (FCA only states that the 2018 Demon's converter stall speed is 11 percent higher than the Hellcat's), lockupTurbineRpm 1,200 rpm and couplingSR 0.90.
